expo.name: Voyage Outdoor
expo._DARK_MODE: userInterfaceStyle is 'automatic' from the first commit, not from Phase 6. VoyageOS is locked to 'light' and has no dark tokens, so every screen written before a dark pass has to be revisited to add one — the retrofit cost the Phase 0 audit flagged. Here the theme ships as a light/dark PAIR and the OS decides.
expo._ICONS: Generated from the brand PDF by scripts/make_icons.py — run it again if the logo changes. The top-level icon is the fallback and carries NO alpha channel: iOS flattens transparency to black, which is how a mark ends up sitting on a black wedge. ios.icon takes the light/dark pair the brand guide already draws ('APP ICON (LIGHT)' on white, 'APP ICON (DARK)' on navy), so those are the designer's intent rather than a guess made here. The Android foreground is sized to the CIRCLE inside the 66% safe zone, not the square — the V's top corners fall outside a square-sized mark on a Pixel.
expo._EXTRA: apiUrl/supabaseUrl/supabaseAnonKey are the three values that flip between dev and production. appKey and scheme must survive any flip. supabaseAnonKey holds the PUBLISHABLE key (sb_publishable_…) — designed to ship in a binary, and it cannot read a table: PostgREST now refuses it outright, so the only thing it opens is /auth/v1. The SECRET key (sb_secret_…) never appears in this file, in the app, or in any build.
